newsitem.title: USA: Saudi holder urges Talley to buy back stock.
newsitem.headline: Saudi holder urges Talley to buy back stock.

text.p: Saudi investor Saad Alissa said Tuesday that he proposed that Talley Industries Inc. use the $172 million it recently received from sales and litigation to buy back at least 7 million shares at $12.11 each in the first quarter.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, a group led by Alissa, who controls 1,121,000 common shares, or 7.55 percent of the total, said he made the proposal in a letter to company Chairman William Mallender.

Under the proposal, the company would conduct a tender offer at $12.11 per share for at least 7 million shares during the first three months of 1997, using the $154 million it received in litigation with TRW Inc. and the $18 million it received from the sale of real estate.
Alissa said he also proposed that the company retain an independent investment banker to value all of the businesses in which Talley Industries engages.
The company's stock was valued at $8 a share, up 50 cents, in midafternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
